# Databasus - PostgreSQL backup tool with MySQL, MariaDB and MongoDB support

> Free, open source and self-hosted tool for scheduled database backups. Save them locally and to clouds, and get notifications in Slack, Discord and other channels.

- License: Apache 2.0
- Repository: [github.com/databasus/databasus](https://github.com/databasus/databasus)
- Website: [databasus.com](https://databasus.com)
- Community: [Telegram chat](https://t.me/databasus_community)
- Developer: Rostislav Dugin, [rostislav-dugin.com](https://rostislav-dugin.com)

## Why Databasus

- **Most widely adopted open-source PostgreSQL backup tool.** As of 17 June 2026 it has over 1,800,000 Docker pulls and 8,500+ GitHub stars, ahead of pgBackRest (~4,200 stars), WAL-G (~4,100) and Barman (~3,100). It has been developed and used since 2023, and in widespread open-source use since early 2025.
- **Built on PostgreSQL's native backup mechanism.** Physical, incremental and WAL backups use PostgreSQL 17's own tools (pg_basebackup, --incremental, pg_receivewal, pg_combinebackup), so it relies on battle-tested tooling instead of a re-invented backup engine. Databasus is the first backup tool built on this standard protocol, and its goal is to become the standard backup tool for PostgreSQL 17 and above.
- **Nothing to install on the database server.** Backups run remotely over the PostgreSQL replication protocol. Closed networks are reached through a built-in SSH tunnel to an internal host or a bastion, so the database is never exposed publicly.
- **Proven restores.** Restore verification restores the latest backup into a real database Docker container and checks it against the source.
- **No vendor lock-in.** Backups can be decrypted and restored with standard tools, without Databasus.
- **Simple to run.** A web UI manages many databases at once, unlike tools that need command-line configuration per database. Installation is zero-config through Docker.
- **Recognized.** In March 2026 Databasus was accepted into both Claude for Open Source by Anthropic and Codex for Open Source by OpenAI. See [OSS programs](https://databasus.com/faq#oss-programs).

## Features

- **Databases:** PostgreSQL 12-18, MySQL 5.7, 8.0, 8.4, 9 and 26, MariaDB 5.5, 10, 11, 12 and 13, MongoDB 4.2+, 5, 6, 7, 8 and 9. PostgreSQL is the primary focus.
- **Schedules:** hourly, daily, weekly, monthly or cron, with an exact run time. Weekly schedules take weekdays, and monthly schedules take calendar days.
- **Storages:** local disk, S3 and S3-compatible services such as Cloudflare R2, Google Drive, NAS, Azure Blob Storage, FTP, SFTP and rclone. Rclone connects 70+ providers, including Dropbox.
- **Notifications:** email, Slack, Telegram, Discord, Microsoft Teams, Mattermost and webhooks.
- **Compression:** balanced compression shrinks dumps 4-8x with about 20% runtime overhead.
- **Encryption:** AES-256-GCM for backup files, useless to attackers even if the storage is compromised.
- **Health checks:** configurable database availability monitoring.
- **Access management:** workspaces, user roles and audit logs for teams.
- **Restore:** one-click restore.

Databasus suits single developers, DevOps teams, startups, system administrators and organizations that need compliance and audit trails.

## Backup types

Every type can run over an SSH tunnel. Physical, full, incremental and WAL backups require PostgreSQL 17 or newer. See [how physical and PITR backups work](https://databasus.com/faq#pitr).

- **Physical:** a file-level copy of the whole cluster, faster to back up and restore for large datasets than logical dumps.
- **Full:** a complete, self-contained copy of the cluster, the base of every backup chain.
- **Incremental:** only what changed since the previous backup, at block level, through PostgreSQL 17 WAL summaries.
- **WAL streaming:** continuous capture of the write stream through pg_receivewal, enabling Point-in-Time Recovery (PITR) to any second, with near-zero data loss.
- **Logical:** a native dump in the engine's binary format, streamed to storage with no intermediate files. It is also the backup type for MySQL, MariaDB and MongoDB.

## Retention policies

Retention runs automatically after each backup.

- **Time period:** keep backups for a fixed duration, such as 7 days or 1 year.
- **Count:** keep a fixed number of the most recent backups, such as the last 30.
- **GFS (Grandfather-Father-Son):** keep hourly, daily, weekly, monthly and yearly backups independently, for long-term compliance history.
- **Size limits:** cap the size per backup and in total.

## Security

All data stays in containers and accounts you control. Three runtime layers protect it: AES-256-GCM encryption of sensitive data, backup encryption with a unique key per backup and read-only database access.

Every commit and pull request also passes engineering checks:

- CodeQL static analysis, gitleaks secret scanning and semgrep security rules;
- Dependabot CVE monitoring with a version cooldown, and the Dependency Review Action failing on HIGH and CRITICAL CVEs;
- Trivy scans of the image on both architectures and of Dockerfiles;
- GitHub Actions pinned to commit SHAs, least-privilege workflow permissions and periodic Codex Security audits from OpenAI;
- integration tests against real database containers for every engine, and full backup-then-restore cycles on every pull request.

See [Security & reliability engineering](https://databasus.com/security#security-and-reliability-engineering).

## Documentation

### Setup

- [Installation](https://databasus.com/installation): automated script, Docker run, Docker Compose and Helm for Kubernetes.
- [Advanced Config](https://databasus.com/advanced-config): optional environment variables for OAuth sign-in, SMTP email, Cloudflare Turnstile, telemetry, OpenTelemetry log export and an analytics script.
- [Access Management](https://databasus.com/access-management): workspaces, roles, audit logs and global settings.
- [Password Reset](https://databasus.com/password): resetting a password with the command-line tool.

### Storages and notifications

- [Storages](https://databasus.com/storages): supported storages and how to configure them.
- [Google Drive](https://databasus.com/storages/google-drive): setup with OAuth.
- [Cloudflare R2](https://databasus.com/storages/cloudflare-r2): S3-compatible storage setup.
- [Notifiers](https://databasus.com/notifiers): supported notification channels and how to configure them.
- [Slack](https://databasus.com/notifiers/slack): webhook setup.
- [Microsoft Teams](https://databasus.com/notifiers/teams): webhook setup.

### Database guides

- [MySQL and MariaDB Backup](https://databasus.com/mysql-backup): mysqldump and mariadb-dump backups, including AWS RDS, Google Cloud SQL, Azure Database for MySQL and PlanetScale.
- [MongoDB Backup](https://databasus.com/mongodb-backup): mongodump backups, including MongoDB Atlas, replica sets and self-hosted deployments.
- [Backing up localhost databases](https://databasus.com/faq/localhost): Docker network setup for a database on the host machine.
- [Backing up Supabase](https://databasus.com/faq/supabase): connecting through the Session Pooler or the IPv4 add-on.

### Restore

- [Restoring without Databasus](https://databasus.com/how-to-recover-without-databasus): decrypting and restoring backups with standard tools and your secret key.
- [Restore Verification](https://databasus.com/restore-verification): the verification agent, resource budgets, schedules and reading results.

### Comparisons

- [Databasus vs pg_dump](https://databasus.com/pgdump-alternative): built on pg_dump, adding a web UI, scheduling, cloud storage, notifications, team features and encryption.
- [Databasus vs pgBackRest](https://databasus.com/databasus-vs-pgbackrest): backup approach, audience, ease of use and recovery options.
- [Databasus vs Barman](https://databasus.com/databasus-vs-barman): backup approach, PITR, ease of use and team features.
- [Databasus vs WAL-G](https://databasus.com/databasus-vs-wal-g): backup approach, multi-database support, ease of use and team features.
- [Databasus vs PgBackWeb](https://databasus.com/databasus-vs-pgbackweb): features, security, team support, storages and notifications.

### Legal and FAQ

- [FAQ](https://databasus.com/faq): backup formats, installation directory, backup types, PITR and disaster recovery.
- [Privacy Policy](https://databasus.com/privacy): covers the website, the self-hosted app with its optional anonymous telemetry and payments through Paddle.
- [Terms of Use](https://databasus.com/terms-of-use): paid services sold through Paddle. The open source software is governed solely by its Apache 2.0 license.

## Installation

- **Requirements:** 1 CPU core, 500 MB RAM, 5 GB plus backup space, Docker Engine 20.10+, Docker Compose v2.0+.
- **Image and defaults:** `databasus/databasus:latest`, port 4005, data in `./databasus-data`, configured through the web UI.
- **Automated script (recommended for Linux):** installs Docker and Docker Compose, sets up auto-restart and uses `/opt/databasus`.
- **Docker run:** a single-command deployment.
- **Docker Compose:** a managed deployment with restart on reboot.
- **Helm:** an official chart from an OCI registry, with a StatefulSet, ClusterIP, LoadBalancer, Ingress or HTTPRoute access, TLS and health probes.
